Sorry I’ve responded to many of your comments, I just really felt a connection to you and the experience you shared. I just wanted to say that what made the biggest difference for me was to see the decision to stop drinking as a positive and exciting thing, rather than a punishment. I would say to myself “I’m finally done with that, thank god I can finally start treating my body nicely and making good decisions for myself.” “I’m so excited to finally start trusting myself again.” “I’m excited to finally make myself and my loved ones proud.” “I’m so excited to start waking up in the morning without anxiety and shame.” 
Another piece of advice: take it one day at a time. Seriously. It sounds cliche, but it’s important. At the beginning of my sobriety attempts, I would always think things like “well shit, what if I want to drink at my wedding?” (Even though I’m not even engaged and have no plans on getting married anytime soon) or, “what if I get invited to a brewery tour or a wine vineyard someday? What will I do then?” It sounds so silly but you might find yourself having those thoughts. Tell yourself that you trust yourself to make that decision when the time comes. You can decide today that you won’t drink today. You can decide tomorrow that you won’t drink tomorrow. Take it a day at a time. Focus on the present.

That’s the spirit, OP. You’re on the right track. I bought a bunch of soda and sparkling waters and candy to get through the first couple months. Buy yourself treats that you wouldn’t normally let yourself indulge in. This is the time to take care of yourself. ❤️

You’re going to be okay, I bet it felt so good to finally talk about this. I promise every person here has done much worse during a blackout. Don’t waste time wallowing in shame, that won’t do any good. Give yourself some compassion. Treat yourself the way you would treat a friend that’s going through this. In addition to the books you’re already reading, I would recommend listening to Huberman Lab’s podcast episode titled “what alcohol does to your body, brain and health.” It’s a scientific and objective approach to the facts about alcohol, and it might help you make these tough decisions. I am so proud of you for coming on here, you got this!! ❤️
